title: Introduce staged fast-lint lanes and dependency-entropy sweeper
text:
Introduce staged fast-lint lanes and dependency-entropy sweeper

description:
Motivation: CI feedback times remain a primary friction for developer velocity. Large monolithic lint/test jobs also amplify noise from transitive dev-dependencies, which leads to CI flakiness and long queue times. This change introduces two coordinated improvements: 1) staged 'fast-lint' lanes that run a focused subset of lint rules and file-scoped checks for immediate feedback, and 2) a dependency-entropy sweeper that automatically detects, tags, and rotates rarely-used transitive dev-deps in CI images, producing a compact dependency profile for fast lanes and a fuller profile for full presubmit runs.

What this PR does: Consolidates lint wiring and introduces stage-aware CI lanes. Specific changes: - Adds new GitHub workflow .github/workflows/fast-lint.yml which executes quick checks (ts/py file-scope lint, type stubs validation, license header) and completes in ~60-90s for most PRs. - Refactors existing lint runner to export a staged interface (tools/ci/lint_runner.ts) so stages can opt-in to heavier rules. - Introduces tools/ci/dep_entropy_sweeper.py which scans package manifests and CI images to compute a 'dep entropy' score and outputs a trimmed lockfile for fast lanes. - Adds a presubmit hook (scripts/ci/trim_lock_for_fast_lane.sh) used by the fast-lint workflow to install a compact devdeps set. - Modifies workflows/presubmit.yml to include an explicit 'full-lint' stage that runs full rules against the canonical lockfile and remains rate-limited to reduce capacity churn. - Adds docs/dev/ci-fastpath.md describing the stage semantics and how to run local sweeper runs.

Design notes: The fast-lint stage is intentionally conservative: it runs a curated rule subset that historically catches ~85% of lint/regression classes while being cheap. The sweeper does not modify source lockfiles — it emits an ephemeral trimmed lockfile committed to the runner workspace for the fast-lane process. The sweeper uses heuristics: usage frequency in the repository, transitive depth, and binary footprint in the runner image. It is designed to be transparent and auditable: logs and the candidate trimmed-manifest are uploaded as artifacts for each presubmit.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the sweeper (tests/dep_sweeper_test.py) and integration smoke for fast-lint on a control PR. CI pipeline changes: fast-lint uses a smaller matrix (node:16, python:3.11) and caches stripped artifacts. Full-lint remains on the larger matrix and still gates merges. During rollout the fast-lint workflow runs as a non-blocking quick feedback lane, then we flip it to required once we have 7 days of stable telemetry.

Rollout plan: Step 1 (this PR merged) enable non-blocking fast-lint across main and non-sensitive repos. Step 2: collect metrics (median feedback time, lint failure concordance) over 7 days. Step 3: if concordance >= 80% and signal stable, mark fast-lint as required for non-critical repos and keep full-lint as required for core packages. Step 4: optionally run sweeper in periodic maintenance jobs to propose lockfile updates and open dep-curation PRs.

Backwards compatibility & safety: The sweeper never rewrites the committed lockfile and the fast-lint uses an ephemeral, runner-local trimmed manifest. Full-lint uses canonical manifests for final validation. All changes are feature-flagged in .github/ci-flags.yml; default is off for required gating.

Related: ENG-5214 (CI velocity), ENG-5290 (dep hygiene), SUP-1127 (incident: flaky dev-image install on worker-5).

Checklist: - [x] fast-lint workflow and docs - [x] lint runner staged interface - [x] dep entropy sweeper + unit tests - [x] integration smoke test - [x] feature flags and rollforward plan

If any reviewer wants the sweeper telemetry for a historical window I can produce a 30-day report (artifact attached to this PR).

release_notes:
Adds a fast, staged lint lane for quick feedback and a new dep-entropy sweeper tool that prunes and rotates transitive devdeps used by CI to reduce flakiness and runtime costs.

discussion_summary:
Consensus: staged fast-lint improves turnaround without weakening safeguards. Sweeper is acceptable under dry-run & artifact auditing. Action items: monitor concordance, optionally tighten fast-lint rule set, and run nightly sweeper proposals.

review_comments:
Rajiv Patel: Can the sweeper run in a dry-run mode for weekly cadence? A: yes — added flag --dry-run and artifact upload (see 9a2f3b6)
Clara Nguyen: I'm worried about flakiness from trimmed lockfiles on macOS dev machines. A: trimmed manifests are CI-only and we added doc notes preventing local install unless explicitly opted-in; full-lint uses canonical manifests.
Owen Gallagher: Suggest reducing node matrix for fast-lint to a single LTS to further cut median runtime. A: reduced to node:16 and documented rationale; can be tuned after telemetry.
CI Bot: e2e failed on first run due to ephemeral cache miss, reran and it passed — recommend increasing cache warming timeout for docker layers.

notes:
Operational note: after merge ops should enable the fast-lint non-blocking flag for the 'redwood' repo, then we will graduate to required once telemetry meets thresholds. The sweeper can be run locally via: python tools/ci/dep_entropy_sweeper.py --repo-root . --output trimmed-lock.json --dry-run
